–Magnification is equal to the distance measured between 2 points on an image divided by the distance between the same 2 points on the original object.–Mag = image distanceobject distance
–Ex: Calculate the magnification of an image where the diameter of the object is 5µmand the diameter on the image is 12.5 mm.–Answer:–Magnification = 12500µm/5µm = –2500X
explanation: This slide provides the mathematical formula for magnification. Magnification is equal to the distance measured between two points on the image divided by the distance between the same two points on the original object (Mag = image distance / object distance). It includes a sample calculation: if the diameter of the original object is 5 µm and its diameter in the image is 12.5 mm (which converts to 12,500 µm), the magnification is 12,500 µm / 5 µm = 2500X.

questions.q: What is the mathematical formula for calculating magnification?
questions.exp: The slide gives the formula: 'Mag = image distance / object distance'.

questions.q: If an object with an actual diameter of 5 µm has a diameter of 12.5 mm on an image, what is the magnification?
questions.exp: First convert 12.5 mm to micrometers: 12.5 mm * 1000 µm/mm = 12500 µm. Then divide by the actual size: 12500 µm / 5 µm = 2500X.
